recognize_zh: 六個小圖中的嗜中性球大小正常、胞質粉紅帶細顆粒，但核只有單一圓形/卵圓形或對稱雙葉，染色質明顯粗糙凝集，呈現假性 Pelger-Huët 異常（pseudo-Pelger-Huët anomaly）；配合移植後用藥史指向藥物引起。
features: Normal-sized neutrophils with pink cytoplasm and fine neutrophilic granules
Nuclei non-lobated (round/ovoid, monolobated) or bilobed/dumbbell-shaped rather than 3-5 lobes
Coarsely clumped, mature-appearing nuclear chromatin despite hypolobation
No obvious cytoplasmic hypogranulation or toxic changes in these cells
Background red cells with crenation; figure composite of six high-power fields with embedded legend
describe_en: Composite peripheral blood smear (Wright stain, high power, panels A-F) shows neutrophils of normal size with pink, finely granular cytoplasm but abnormal nuclear segmentation, including monolobated cells with a single round to ovoid nucleus and bilobed dumbbell-shaped forms. Chromatin is coarsely clumped, indicating nuclear maturity despite hypolobation, which distinguishes these cells from myelocytes. Cytoplasmic granulation appears preserved. Findings are consistent with pseudo-Pelger-Huët anomaly, which in this post-transplant patient receiving mycophenolate mofetil and ganciclovir is compatible with a drug effect, although myelodysplasia must be excluded clinically.

ddx.vs: The inherited LBR-related form affects nearly all neutrophils with uniform bilobed spectacle-shaped nuclei, normal counts and a family history, whereas acquired forms involve a subset of cells and resolve on drug withdrawal.
MDS often shows pseudo-Pelger cells with cytoplasmic hypogranulation, other dysplastic lineages and cytogenetic abnormalities, requiring marrow examination to separate it from drug effect.
Immature granulocytes have finer, less condensed chromatin and more basophilic cytoplasm with primary granules, unlike the densely clumped chromatin of pseudo-Pelger neutrophils.
Bands have an elongated, curved, sausage-shaped nucleus of uniform width, not a round or symmetric dumbbell nucleus.
